analysis.title: Equinor 3Qs, Ras Tanura hit + Oil & Gas Daily 28/10/26
key_insights: Houthis claim a missile hit on Saudi Arabia's 550kb/d Ras Tanura refinery. Brent touched $116/b. Saudi Aramco has not confirmed the attack.

UBS spec sales says the claimed attack underscores the difficulty of progress towards a ceasefire. Khamenei reiterated Iran's conditions for ending the war, which have not changed materially since the MoU failed earlier this year.

Israel's parliamentary election (yesterday) and the US midterms are the most important imminent oil catalysts. Reports suggest the US and Israel may prepare a short but intense military escalation after the midterms to pressure Iran.

WSJ reports the US told several Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the midterms. This puts escalation risk on a dated horizon. Crude was up 1.5-2% (WTI $101.5, Brent $115.8).

Equinor 3Q26 operating earnings of $12.4bn were a 1% beat and adjusted operating profit of $3.53bn was a 4% beat. Financial items drove a 15% miss at net income. CFFO ex working capital of $8.1bn was a 1% beat.

Equinor's marketing, midstream and processing segment beat by 13% on refining and gas trading. Gearing fell to 3.8% vs UBSe 6.3%. FY production guidance was raised to 4% growth from 3%. Distributions are unchanged and the next buyback tranche is confirmed.
UBS spec sales prefers leverage to high EU natural gas. QatarEnergy extended force majeure with Italy's Edison to at least end December.

UBS base case for this evening's FOMC is a hold by a 10-2 vote, with Warsh hawkish ('more work to do'). UBS expects 25bp hikes in December and January. Markets price about a 10% chance of an October hike, 92% for a 25bp December hike and 33bps cumulative by January.
Equities: S&P +60bps, Nasdaq +1.2%, SOX and memory +3-3.5%. KOSPI rose about 7% after SK Hynix's Q3 print and a capital return of about 100tn won (~$45bn). SK Hynix shares rose 10% and Samsung 8%.

TAIEX rose 2% on OpenAI and Oracle partnerships with Google (MediaTek +7%, TSMC +1%). TSMC is reported to be lifting advanced packaging prices by 20% on AI demand. GOOG and MSFT results after the close are called pivotal.

UK Autumn Budget is expected to be cautious. Fiscal headroom may have fallen from £23.6bn in March to about £10bn, with a modest buffer of about £15bn rebuilt through smaller tax increases. UBS sees support for gilts, resilient GBP and selective equity opportunities in housebuilders, property, lower-value consumer and public-investment names.
UK bank levy: verbal consensus is a move towards 8% from 3%. UBS models 3% to 6%, implying a 3-4% cut to NWG/LLOY numbers and 1-2% to BARC/HSBC numbers.

European flows on Tuesday were better to buy (54/46), with participation about 30% above the YTD run rate. Technology was 16% of turnover and balanced, Industrials 14% and better bid, Banks 14% with demand in French and UK names. Healthcare and Energy saw demand. Telecoms, Food & Bev, Utilities and Insurance saw supply.
API data: US crude stocks fell 2.03M barrels in the week ended October 23, gasoline rose about 2.39M and distillates rose about 426K.
Russian refineries raised crude processing 25% in the second half of October after Ukrainian drone attacks stopped following the Oct 11 'energy ceasefire'. No strikes were reported after Oct 16.

Trump proposed scaling back methane rules, citing $45bn in cost savings. France will release 10M barrels of diesel from strategic reserves from November 1. Diesel prices have hit record highs in many markets.
Expand Energy beat 3Q adjusted EPS at $1.46 vs LSEG consensus $1.27. Mitsubishi Power says gas turbine deliveries are being pushed out to about 2031.
Dangote's refinery IPO drew about three times the targeted orders (6.4 trillion naira, ~$4.78bn). A greenshoe could lift the offering to as much as $2.1bn.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 was a small beat with production guidance raised to 4% from 3%. UBS spec sales prefers leverage to high EU natural gas.
3Q production and CFPS beat was offset by higher capex. Near-term drivers are marketing growth and the arrival of a new CEO.
Adjusted EBITDA beat the Street by 5%. The Horizon 2 IET order target was raised by another $5Bn to over $50Bn.
3Q update was positive on capital efficiency and liquids growth, attributes that made it appealing to EQT.
Neutral update following the transaction announcement, as lower costs offset production curtailments.
Quarterly dividend raised 12.5% to $1.211, with UBS expecting another 12.5% distribution increase in 2027. Positive for parent MPC.
MPLX covers its dividend and full capex for the parent.
UBS highlights three growth projects (SEC, Permian Link and 219 South), which were recently approved for investment.
ADNOC Drilling 3Q26 numbers were broadly in line. Guidance was narrowed to the lower end and a surprise special dividend was announced.
Adecoagro 3Q26 preview points to a more than 20% free cash flow yield in 2027E.

sector_views.rationale: Selective opportunities in housebuilders, property, lower-value consumer names and public-investment beneficiaries, not a broad UK equity rerating.
UBS spec sales prefers leverage to high EU natural gas, and the desk notes demand for Energy in European flows.

earnings_insights: Equinor 3Q26 reported: operating earnings $12.4bn, a 1% beat vs UBS expectations. Adjusted operating profit $3.53bn, a 4% beat. Net income missed by 15% on financial items. CFFO ex working capital $8.1bn, a 1% beat.
Equinor 3Q26 reported: marketing, midstream and processing beat by 13% on refining and gas trading. Gearing was 3.8% vs UBSe 6.3%. FY production guidance was raised to 4% growth from 3%.
Expand Energy reported 3Q adjusted EPS of $1.46 vs LSEG analyst average estimate of $1.27. UBS notes the production and CFPS beat was offset by higher capex.
Baker Hughes reported 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA 5% above Street. Its Horizon 2 IET order target was raised by $5Bn to over $50Bn.
ONEOK reported a modest 3Q26 beat and raised guidance.
MPLX raised its quarterly dividend 12.5% to $1.211.
ADNOC Drilling 3Q26 reported numbers broadly in line, guidance narrowed to the lower end of its range, with a surprise special dividend.
Range Resources 3Q26 update was positive on capital efficiency and liquids growth. EQT 3Q26: lower costs offset production curtailments.
Nabors signed a multi-year contract to deploy one rig in Venezuela in early 2027, disclosed in its third quarter results.
SK Hynix reported a Q3 print described as a blowout with a capital return of about 100tn won (~$45bn). Adecoagro 3Q26 preview points to a more than 20% free cash flow yield in 2027E.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Oil rose on the claimed Houthi strike on Ras Tanura and the WSJ report of a possible post-midterm US military campaign.
Crude was up 1.5-2% on the day.
Crude drew, while gasoline rose about 2.39M and distillates rose about 426K.
UBS expects a hawkish hold with Warsh saying there is more work to do on inflation.
Markets price about 92% for a December hike and 33bps cumulatively by January.
UBS describes it as sticky rather than accelerating.
A cautious budget is expected, with a buffer of about £15bn rebuilt and maintained fiscal rules supportive for gilts.

trade_ideas.description: Long leverage to high EU natural gas via Equinor
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS spec sales prefers leverage to high EU natural gas, noting Qatar LNG force majeure is extended through December.

risk_factors: Escalation in the Iran war, including a US-Israeli military campaign after the midterms.
Unconfirmed Houthi strike on Ras Tanura adds supply risk and could widen regional conflict.
A hawkish FOMC with hikes expected in December and January.
UK bank levy rising towards 8% and a cautious UK Budget.
GOOG and MSFT results after the close are pivotal for tech sentiment.
vol_and_positioning: The desk notes market sensitivity to oil headlines looks lower on a day-to-day basis and expects Tech/Nasdaq/AI to grind higher as earnings restore sentiment.
European flow on Tuesday finished better to buy (54/46) with participation about 30% above the YTD run rate.
geopolitical: Houthis claim a ballistic missile hit on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, causing a fire. Saudi authorities have not confirmed it. The Iran war began eight months ago.
Houthis also claim attacks on Saudi military aircraft and to have repelled a Saudi-backed advance near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei reiterated Iran's conditions for ending the war, unchanged since the MoU failed.
WSJ reports the US told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the US midterms.
Qatar extended LNG force majeure to Italy's Edison through at least end December.
Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on October 11. Russian refinery output is recovering.
First Venezuelan crude under the US-NABEP deal arrived in Texas for sale to Exxon and Citgo refineries.
US midterms on November 3 and Israel's parliamentary election are the key political catalysts.

tension_points.bull_case: Market sensitivity to oil headlines appears lower day to day, and UBS expects Tech/Nasdaq/AI to grind higher on earnings delivery.
tension_points.bear_case: The WSJ report of a short, intense US campaign after the midterms, plus the claimed Ras Tanura hit, puts escalation risk on a dated horizon and complicates ceasefire progress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Israel's election result and the US midterms (November 3) are named as the key catalysts, and GOOG and MSFT results after the close are called pivotal for tech sentiment.
